title: Claude Code routines are now scheduled tasks: a guide
h1: claude code routines are now called scheduled tasks
description: Understand Claude Code cloud scheduled tasks, local tasks and /loop, including what runs with your laptop closed and how Dusk routines differ.
answer: claude code routines are now called cloud scheduled tasks. you save a prompt, repositories and connectors, then run that setup on a schedule, through an api call or from a github event. as of 12 november 2026, they run on anthropic-managed infrastructure and are marked research preview. local desktop tasks and the /loop command are different: they depend on your computer staying awake.[^1][^2][^3]
og_line: three ways to repeat, with different homes.

sections.md:
a prompt is the job you want done. a repository is the project material for a code task. connectors give access to connected systems. a cloud scheduled task saves those choices together so you do not reconstruct the setup for every run.[^1]

for a non-developer, the first decision is whether the work belongs with a code project at all. a recurring review of project changes may fit that structure. a general household reminder may not need it. the name "scheduled task" describes repetition, not a guarantee that the saved task has the context or permissions needed to complete your work.

sections.h: where to create one, and what is limited
sections.md:
anthropic documents creation at **claude.ai/code/routines** or with **/schedule** in the cli. the address still contains the old name. as of 12 november 2026, availability is pro, max, ultra, team and enterprise, and the feature is a research preview.[^1]

the documented minimum interval for cloud tasks is **one hour**. the account limit is **100 scheduled runs per hour**. run now, api fires and re-running one-off tasks have a **30 per hour per task** limit. runs consume plan usage. those figures describe different limits, so do not read the account ceiling as permission to run a single recurring task every minute.[^1]

sections.h: cloud tasks, local tasks and loop
sections.md:
- **cloud scheduled tasks:** run on anthropic-managed infrastructure and continue when your laptop is closed.[^1]
- **desktop local scheduled tasks:** have direct access to your machine's files and tools, but fire only while the app is open and the computer is awake.[^2]
- **/loop:** repeats a prompt inside an open claude code session, with a minimum interval of one minute. the machine must stay on.[^3]

choose the place the material lives before choosing the interval. a local folder and a cloud repository are different inputs. the [laptop-closed guide](/agents-when-laptop-closed) explains why the location of the running program matters. a timer cannot keep a sleeping local process working.

sections.h: cowork scheduled tasks are another feature to recognize
sections.md:
anthropic also documents scheduled tasks in cowork and the new claude experience. those run saved prompts remotely, including while the computer sleeps. tasks created before 6 october that run on the computer keep running there. each run is its own session and can use connectors, skills and plugins.[^4]

the [claude scheduled tasks guide](/guides/claude-scheduled-tasks) covers that product path. do not combine instructions for all the schedulers into one tutorial. first identify whether you are looking at a code cloud task, a code desktop task, /loop, or a task in claude's knowledge-work experience.

sections.h: dusk routines start with a message
sections.md:
in dusk bot, a routine is a job a bot does without being asked again. tell it the job and timing in plain words. the bot returns a card showing the schedule and next runs, with **Edit**, **Pause** and **Undo**. **Automations** lists routines with a calendar and run history.[^5]

a routine can also start from an event in a connected app. on your own computer, nothing runs while it sleeps or dusk bot is closed. a run missed by less than 12 hours runs once when you return; older missed runs are skipped. dusk cloud runs them on time. [scheduled ai tasks](/scheduled-ai-tasks) helps compare what you need to keep awake.[^5]

sections.h: review the result before making it recurring
sections.md:
write a narrow job with its input, destination and reason to stay quiet. try the underlying task once and check its sources. if the result is missing context, fix that before adding a schedule.

in dusk bot, read-only app access is the strongest starting boundary for a reading routine. if you later allow app changes, include "ask me before you change anything" when you want them supervised. sends have their own approval rule, unless you choose a daily amount. one exception: a bot on **Full access** with no sending rule of its own may send up to 25 a day without asking, so give full-access bots **Ask every time** under sending. repetition should not quietly turn a trial into broader authority.[^6]

faq.q: will claude code routines work with my laptop closed?
faq.a: cloud scheduled tasks do. desktop local tasks and /loop depend on the local machine and session requirements. the current names matter when comparing tutorials.[^1][^2][^3]

faq.q: can i run a cloud scheduled task every minute?
faq.a: the documented minimum cloud interval is one hour. /loop has a one-minute minimum but runs inside an open local session, so it solves a different problem.[^1][^3]

faq.q: do i need cron to make a dusk routine?
faq.a: no. describe the repeating job to the bot and review the schedule card it returns. you can edit or pause it from there.[^5]
